==Problem==

Each principal of Lincoln High School serves exactly one <imath>3</imath>-year term. What is the maximum number of principals this school could have during an <imath>8</imath>-year period?

<imath>\text{(A)}\ 2 \qquad \text{(B)}\ 3 \qquad \text{(C)}\ 4 \qquad \text{(D)}\ 5 \qquad \text{(E)}\ 8</imath>

==Solution 1==

Suppose the current principal's term will end in <imath>1</imath> year.  Of the next <imath>8</imath> years, the current principal will serve the first year; the next principal will serve the second, third, and fourth years; a third principal will serve the fifth, sixth, and seventh years; and a fourth principal will serve the eighth year.  Therefore, <imath>4</imath> different principals will serve in the next <imath>8</imath> years.

Consider a period that includes at least <imath>5</imath> different principals.  During this period, all principals except the first and last must serve complete terms. So at least <imath>3</imath> principals serve complete terms, and thus this period is at least <imath>9</imath> years long.  Therefore, an <imath>8</imath>-year period may not have <imath>5</imath> or more different principals.

Thus there can be at most <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(C)}\ 4}</imath> principals in an <imath>8</imath>-year period.

==Solution 2==

In an <imath>8</imath>-year period, at most <imath>\left\lfloor{\frac{8}{3}}\right\rfloor = 2</imath> principals could serve complete terms.  Furthermore, at most <imath>2</imath> principals could serve incomplete terms during this period: those who are in office at the start and end of this period.  Therefore, at most <imath>2 + 2 = \boxed{\textbf{(C)}\ 4}</imath> principals could be active during this period (which would happen if the acting principal at the start of the period has <imath>1</imath> year left of their term).
